unit.why: A narrative quoted from Siddur Nehora ha-Shalem: the author of Zera Yitzhak hears the heavenly court judge a departed righteous man. It is a pre-Hasidic moral exemplum about uttering God's name in vain, not a tale about Hasidic figures.

stories.start_quote: בסידור נהורא השלם וז"ל מצאתי שהמחבר
stories.summary_en: The author of Zera Yitzhak was drawn up and heard the heavenly court judge a departed righteous man: angels born of his mitzvot testified for him, but black-clad destroying angels created by his uttering God's names in prayer without intention testified against him, and he was sentenced to choose between Gehinnom and reincarnation, choosing Gehinnom.

quotes: ובאו המלאכים שנבראו מהמצות אשר עשה
ובאו גדודי מלאכי חבלה לבושים ומתעטפים שחורים
tags.why: Angels created from his mitzvot and destroying angels testify
The whole scene takes place in the heavenly court

quotes: ושמע בב״ד של מעלה קול רעש גדול
tags.why: A heavenly beit din holds legal proceedings with witnesses and a verdict

quotes: או לירד לגיהנם או יחזור ויבוא בגלגול
tags.why: Gehinnom is the sentenced destination, though not shown as a setting
Reincarnation is offered as an alternative punishment
The man is sentenced for his transgression
The prohibition on uttering God's name in vain is the crux

quotes: כשהוציא כך וכך אזכר״ת בתפלה בלא כוונה
tags.why: His sin was saying divine names in prayer without intention
The judgment follows the man's death

quotes: שהמחבר זרע יצחק ז"ל אנגיד ושמע בב״ד של מעלה
tags.why: The author was 'drawn up' and witnessed the heavenly court

quotes: ושמע בב״ד של מעלה קול רעש גדול
tags.why: He hears heavenly voices and proceedings
Copied from an older book about a pre-Hasidic author's experience, though it does not mainly praise him
Functions as a moral warning against uttering God's name in vain

quotes: ושאלוהו קיימת תורה בע״פ ואמר הן
tags.why: His observance of the Shulhan Arukh and specific commandments is examined
He is rebuked for lacking fear of God

missing_concepts: heavenly trial / posthumous judgment of the soul
angels created from mitzvot and sins (advocates and accusers)
